lawyer:
MI Chowdhury, Advocate—For the Petitioners. 
KS Nabi, Attorney-General with AM Aminuddin, Assistant Attorney-General — For the Respondents.
parties:
Rehana Kamal and another ------ Petitioners
Vs. 
Chairman Court of Settlement and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 11. We are unable to accept the submission of the learned Attorney-General. The properties in question admittedly were allotted to Dr. Mahmood Hasan and Dr. Mahmood Hasan constructed a building there on and died in December 25, 1970 in Karachi. Before death he distributed all his properties to his wife, daughters and sons, who accepted the same and his two daughters namely; Rehana Kamal and Rifat Alam were given the building in question in equal share which has been accepted by other co-sharers and there is no dispute. It appears that in the affidavit-in-opposition it is also admitted by the Government that Dr. Mahmood Hasan died in Karachi on 25-11-70 leaving behind Rifat Alam and Mrs Rehana Kamal amongst other legal heirs as two daughters. In fact there is no denial about acquiring property by two sisters by gift from their father Dr. Mahmood Hasan and there is no denial that before creation of Bangladesh Dr. Mahmood Hasan died in December, 25th, 1970 in Karachi and before his death he gifted the property in question to his 2 daughters namely, petitioner No. 1 and mother of petitioner No. 2 and also there is no denial by any affidavit-in-opposition that both the sisters were accepted as landladies by the tenant American Embassy who was inducted by their father. There is also no denial that they mutated their names with the Dhaka Municipality and paid rent and taxes, etc. Then there is no denial by any affidavit to the assertion made in supplementary affidavit that the petitioner No. 1 and her sister, mother of petitioner No. 2, were stranded in Pakistan and thereafter managed to escape to Germany and Canada in 1973 and furthermore, there is no denial by any affidavit that the tenant American Embassy paid rent to them and the rents were deposited in the Joint SB Account of the 2 sisters with American Express Bank situated at Alico Building, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka. Mr. Attorney-General simply argued on presumption that they are not Bangladeshi Nationals but could not show anything that they obtained citizenship of a country which was at war with Bangladesh, or the two sisters in any way engaged in any prejudicial activities against Bangladesh. It appears that Dr. Mahmood Hasan before his death on December 25th, 1970 gifted his properties to his heirs and the property in question fell in the share of the 2 daughters, petitioner No. 1 and mother of petitioner No. 2 and the American Embassy inducted as tenant by their father, accepted them as their landladies and none of the other heirs of Dr. Mahmood Hasan raised any objection. It appears that in the year 1970 the lease agreement was further renewed for 2 years more and the American Embassy accepting both the sisters as land ledies paid .them rent for 1 year in advance amounting to Taka 24,000.00 @ of Taka 2000.00 per month. In the meantime Rifat Alam, sister of petitioner No. 1 gifted her share to his son Syed Ayyad Alam petitioner No. 2 and to manage their properties both the sisters executed general power of attorney appointing Mrs. Anwari Begum and Mrs Syeda Sajada Chowdhury on 27-12-88 and 28-11-88 respectively. It further appears from the record of the Government annexed hereto the Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Works wrote a letter under Memo No. 2F-III-156/73/8 dated 23-10-73 to the American Embassy informing them that the legal status of the house is under examination in the Ministry of Law and in this circumstances they may choose not to pay rent to the absentee owners, their Attorneys or agents until further communications from the Ministry. From this letter it is abundantly clear that whereabouts of the owners were very much known to the Ministry and also they had attorneys, agents to manage this properties etc. vide Annexure-M. The Assistant Administrative Officer of the Embassy duly informed Mrs. Anowari Begum, constituted attorney of one of the owners, about the letter. Then again, on 20-11-73 one Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Works wrote to the Assistant Administrative Officer of the Embassy informing that he was directed to advise that pending decision of the legal status of the property in question within the meaning of Article 2 of the President''s Order 16 of 1972 the Ministry allowed the Embassy to stay in the house. But when the legal status was not decided for two years thereafter then the Embassy on 31-12-75 wrote a letter to the Secretary, Ministry of Works to look into the matter to decide the status of the house. In the year 1976 Mahmud Kamal, husband of the petitioner No. 1, came to Bangladesh from Germany and met the Secretary, Ministry of Works on 7-5-76 with a written representation to him with a prayer to hand over the property; Annexure-O and since the legal status of the house was thus pending the attorneys of Mrs Rehana Kamal and Mrs. Rifat Alam wanted to pay revenue, tax etc. but the Government refused to accept on the ground that the house has been declared as abandoned property and the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka advised them in writing on 6-1-91 to contact with the Management Board of the abandoned property as it was published in the Gazette Extra-ordinary as abandoned building in the Ka list at page 9762 dated 23-9-86. Thereafter the petitioner No. 2 came to Bangladesh from Canada knowing that his house was declared abandoned property and a Settlement Court was established to try the abandoned cases and instructed the attorneys to apply before respondent No. 1 for exclusion of the building from the list and it was numbered as 3/92 which was dismissed along with 22 other petitions on the ground of limitation. Admittedly till 31st December, 1975 the legal status of the property was not decided by the Government. The President''s Order 16 of 1972 came into force on 28-2-72 and all properties abandoned on or before 25th March, 71 vest in the Government to deal with the administrative control, management and disposal of or otherwise in accordance with the provision of this Order but admittedly from the Annexures-M, N, O, P it appears that the Government could not decide till 31st December, 1975 what will be the status of the property. Only thing they said that the legal status of the property in question was under consideration of the Ministry of Law. From such facts it appears admittedly till 31-12-75 no opinion could be formed by the Government. In the case referred above reported in 28 DLR (AD) 120 and 27 DLR 170 wherein it has been held to declare the property as abandoned Government is to form an opinion that the owner of the property is not in Bangladesh his or whereabouts are not known or who has ceased to occupy, supervise or manage the property before declaring the property as abandoned. On the formation of opinion by the Government the definition clause comes into operation. The petitioner''s positive case is that they are in possession of the property in question through their tenants and also the assertion of the petitioners that their whereabouts were very much known to the Government have not been denied by the Government by any affidavit.
